name: Caro-Kann Defense
description: Rock-solid defence: 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5, with the light-squared bishop developed outside the pawn chain.

lines.name: Short System

notes.1: …c6 prepares …d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's path open, unlike the French.
notes.5: …Bf5 develops the bishop outside the chain before …e6 shuts it in.
notes.9: …c5 hits d4, the base of White's pawn chain, as in the French.
notes.10: Be3 defends d4, but the bishop no longer guards b2.
notes.11: …Qb6 hits b2 and adds a second attacker on d4.

11.Nc6: dxc5! wins a pawn, and the e3 bishop guards it.

lines.summary: Get the bishop out to f5 first, then …e6, …c5 and …Qb6 to hit d4 and b2.

lines.name: Short, 6.c3

notes.1: …c6 prepares …d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's path open, unlike the French.
notes.5: …Bf5 develops the bishop outside the chain before …e6 shuts it in.
notes.9: …c5 hits d4, the base of White's pawn chain, as in the French.
notes.11: …Nc6 adds a second attacker on d4.

lines.summary: Against c3, keep piling up on d4 with …Nc6, then …Qb6.

lines.name: Short, 6.O-O

notes.1: …c6 prepares …d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's path open, unlike the French.
notes.5: …Bf5 develops the bishop outside the chain before …e6 shuts it in.
notes.9: …c5 hits d4, the base of White's pawn chain, as in the French.
notes.11: …Nc6 adds a second attacker on d4.

lines.summary: Against 6.O-O, develop with …Nc6 and keep hitting d4.

lines.name: Short: 5.Bd3

notes.1: …c6 prepares …d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's path open, unlike the French.
notes.5: …Bf5 develops the bishop outside the chain before …e6 shuts it in.
notes.9: …Bxd3 trades off White's best attacking bishop.
notes.11: …c5 hits d4 at once, as in the French.

lines.summary: When White offers the bishop trade with Bd3, take it and hit d4 with …c5.

lines.name: 4.Bd3

notes.1: …c6 prepares …d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's path open, unlike the French.
notes.5: …Bf5 develops the bishop outside the chain before …e6 shuts it in.
notes.7: …Bxd3 swaps off Black's problem bishop, the usual worry in French-type structures.
notes.11: …c5 strikes at the base of the chain; this is the 5.Bd3 position again.

lines.summary: 4.Bd3 lets you trade your bad bishop; then hit d4 with …e6 and …c5.

lines.name: Classical (4…Bf5)

notes.1: …c6 prepares …d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's path open, unlike the French.
notes.7: …Bf5 develops with tempo on the e4 knight.
notes.11: …Nd7 stops Ne5 and prepares …Ngf6 without allowing a pawn-breaking Nxf6+.
notes.13: …h6 keeps a retreat square for the bishop, so h5 doesn't trap it.
notes.15: …Bh7 keeps the bishop alive on its diagonal; White has spent time on h-pawn moves.

lines.summary: Bishop to f5, then g6 and h7: answer the h-pawn march with …h6 and keep the bishop.

lines.name: 11.Bd2

notes.1: …c6 prepares …d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's path open, unlike the French.
notes.7: …Bf5 develops with tempo on the e4 knight.
notes.11: …Nd7 stops Ne5 and prepares …Ngf6 without allowing a pawn-breaking Nxf6+.
notes.13: …h6 keeps a retreat square for the bishop, so h5 doesn't trap it.
notes.15: …Bh7 keeps the bishop alive on its diagonal; White has spent time on h-pawn moves.
notes.17: …Bxd3 trades the good bishop for White's; Black's position is solid but a little passive.
notes.19: …e6 opens the f8 bishop; the black king will castle short or stay in the centre.
notes.21: …Ngf6 develops the last knight, eyeing e4 and g4.
notes.23: …Be7 prepares …O-O; the h5 pawn can become a target later.

lines.summary: Trade light-squared bishops, then develop quietly with …e6, …Ngf6 and …Be7.

lines.name: 6.Nf3 Nd7 7.Bd3

notes.1: …c6 prepares …d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's path open, unlike the French.
notes.7: …Bf5 develops with tempo on the e4 knight.
notes.11: …Nd7 stops Ne5 and prepares …Ngf6 without allowing a pawn-breaking Nxf6+.
notes.13: …e6: if White takes on g6, Black recaptures towards the centre with the h-pawn.

lines.summary: Against 7.Bd3, play …e6 and let White decide about the bishops.

lines.name: 6.h4 move order

notes.1: …c6 prepares …d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's path open, unlike the French.
notes.7: …Bf5 develops with tempo on the e4 knight.
notes.11: …h6 keeps a retreat square for the bishop, so h5 doesn't trap it.
notes.15: …Bh7: the same position as the 6.Nf3 order.

lines.summary: If White starts with h4, answer …h6, then …Nd7 and …Bh7 as usual.

lines.name: Exchange Variation

notes.1: …c6 prepares …d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's path open, unlike the French.
notes.5: …cxd5 gives Black the half-open c-file for the queenside play.
notes.11: …Bg4 develops the bishop actively before …e6 locks it in.
notes.13: …Qd7 defends b7 along the seventh rank.
notes.15: …e6 opens the f8 bishop; next come …Bd6 and castling.

lines.summary: Develop the bishop to g4 before …e6, guard b7 with …Qd7, then play on the c-file.

lines.name: 9.Ngf3

notes.1: …c6 prepares …d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's path open, unlike the French.
notes.5: …cxd5 gives Black the half-open c-file for the queenside play.
notes.11: …Bg4 develops the bishop actively before …e6 locks it in.
notes.13: …Qd7 defends b7 along the seventh rank.
notes.15: …e6 opens the f8 bishop; next come …Bd6 and castling.
notes.17: …Bd6 challenges White's good bishop on f4.
notes.19: …Qxd6 recaptures and keeps the queen central.
notes.21: …O-O: next Black plays on the queenside with …Rab8 and …b5.

lines.summary: Trade dark-squared bishops, castle, then push …b5-b4 on the queenside (a minority attack).

lines.name: Panov Attack (4.c4)

notes.1: …c6 prepares …d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's path open, unlike the French.
notes.5: …cxd5 gives Black the half-open c-file for the queenside play.
notes.7: …Nf6 hits d5 and develops; White aims for an isolated d-pawn position.
notes.9: …e6 supports d5 and opens the f8 bishop.
notes.13: …Nxd5 puts the knight on a strong central square in front of White's isolated pawn.

9.Bf5: Qb3! hits b7 and d5 at once.

lines.summary: Against the isolated d-pawn, blockade d5 with a knight and trade pieces.

lines.name: 2.Nf3

notes.1: …c6 prepares …d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's path open, unlike the French.
notes.3: …d5: the usual Caro-Kann answer; after exd5 cxd5 and d4 it's an Exchange.
notes.7: …Nc6 develops and puts pressure on d4.

lines.summary: Against 2.Nf3, still play …d5; after exd5 cxd5 and d4, develop with …Nc6 and …Nf6.
